description: CPhL hockey from Coldwater, called by Tug Brennan. A fresh sixty minutes is simulated every airing.
name: Cluster Puck: CPhL Coldwater Hockey

boards: {hitter} finishes {victim} into the boards and the glass takes the rest.
RIDDEN INTO THE BOARDS. {hitter} on {victim}, and that whole pane is still moving.
{victim} gets caught with his head down and {hitter} puts him through the dasher.
Big hit, {hitter}. {victim} will get up from that one. Probably.
boards.behind: From behind. {hitter} runs {victim} face first into the boards, and nobody in stripes saw a thing.
{victim} never saw {hitter} coming, because {hitter} came from behind. Numbers to the boards and straight in.
That's a hit from behind, {hitter} on {victim}, and the dasher has his face on it now.
boards.elbow: Elbow up, and {hitter} leaves it in {victim}'s face on the way past.
{hitter} leads with the elbow and {victim}'s head goes back into the boards. An assault anywhere else. Legal here.
That's an elbow, high, {hitter} on {victim}, and the helmet's going one way and {victim} the other.
boards.glass: {hitter} puts {victim} into the glass at full speed, and the glass very nearly lets him through.
THE GLASS. {hitter} on {victim}, and the people in the front row just got a good look at his face.
{victim} goes into the pane head first courtesy of {hitter}. That's a crack they'll be looking at all period.
boards.hip: {hitter} drops the hip and {victim} goes right over the top of him, skates in the air.
HIP CHECK. {victim} upended by {hitter}, cartwheels, lands on his neck. The building loves it.
{victim} cuts to the middle and {hitter} hips him into next week. Feet over head.
chatter: The ice in here hasn't been resurfaced since the ownership change, and you can tell; {team} are skating through what I'd generously call a puddle with ambition.
Goal judge's been in that booth thirty years. Nobody's checked on him in twelve. Light still works.
{goalie} has the thousand-yard stare of a man watching his own future arrive on a two-on-one.
The Zamboni runs on something the league won't disclose and the driver wears a respirator. Draw your own conclusions.
Nobody founded this league. The scheduler just started sending pairings one morning and the clubs turned up. Forty years later here we all are.
That's the third time tonight someone's gone head first into the boards and the third time the officials have looked at their shoes.
They sell a hot dog here that's legally not a hot dog. There's a sign. Nobody reads the sign.
I'm told the trophy is a pre-Handoff vessel of unknown industrial purpose. They fill it. They drink from it. Champions do tend to die.
The {team} bench is quiet. Then again half of them are hurt and one of them is, I believe, technically deceased.
There's a man in section nine who has come to every home game for nineteen years and has never cheered.
Attendance tonight is announced as capacity, which it always is, because nobody counts.
Somewhere in this building is a room with all the league's records in it. Nobody has ever found the door.
The glass behind that net has been replaced four times this season. Same pane. Same corner. Same reason.
{shooter} came up through the Ashway. You can tell by the way he skates like the ice owes him money.
It's fourteen below out there and colder in here, which is a choice somebody made deliberately.
The CPhL doesn't have a commissioner. It has a scheduler, and the scheduler has never been late.
chatter.docks: You can hear the cranes through the roof here. Third period, low tide, the whole building hums.
The Docks barn floods twice a winter. They play through it. There is a line painted on the wall showing how high, and it is above my head.
Half this crowd came straight off a shift and half of them are still wearing the hard hats. The hats are not for the hockey.
cup.final: THE {leader} HAVE WON THE COLDWATER CUP. {home} {homeScore}, {away} {awayScore}. They'll drink out of it, because that's the tradition, and we'll see who's still here next season.
IT'S OVER. The {leader} are your Coldwater Cup champions. Carve it into whatever's still standing.
cup.intro: This is it. The Coldwater Cup. Nobody can produce a record of who commissioned it, and the one reporter who went looking took a job in Terminus instead.
Cup final tonight. One game, one trophy, and a trophy nobody can explain.
cup.matchup: For the Coldwater Cup: the {away} against the {home}.
{away} and {home}, for the Cup. Whatever it originally held, it holds champagne tonight.
cup.outro: Coldwater Cup champions, the {leader}. Enjoy it. Historically, that has been the advice.
The {leader} take the Cup. I'm Tug Brennan, and I'd let it air out before you drink from it.
death: {player} IS DEAD. That's the game: sudden death, and the CPhL has never pretended it meant anything else. {winnerTeam} win it.
He's gone. {player}, on the ice, in overtime, and that's how this league ends a tie.
{player} doesn't get up, and he isn't going to. {winnerTeam} take it. Somebody call his people.
death.wound: {wound}. Nobody needs the doctor to tell them.
{wound}. They're putting a towel over him now.
{wound}. The building has gone completely quiet.
faceoff: Clean draw, and away we go.
Won back cleanly, and the {winTeam} have it.
faceoff.center: Back to centre ice. {winner} takes the draw from {loser} and the {winTeam} have it.
Centre-ice draw, and {winner} wins it clean. {winTeam} puck.
They line it up at centre. {winner} beats {loser} to it and away we go.
Puck's down at centre. {winTeam} come away with it.
faceoff.neutral: Neutral-zone draw. {winner} ties up {loser} and the {winTeam} come away with it.
Dropped outside the line, and {winner} wins it.
{winner} takes the neutral-zone draw. Nothing much happens here and that's the point.
faceoff.zone: Draw in the {zone}. {winner} wins it back for the {winTeam}.
Down in the {zone}, and {winner} takes it off {loser}.
They set up in the {zone}. {winner} gets a stick on it first and it's {winTeam} possession.
{winner} wins the draw deep. That's {foAway}–{foHome} on the dot tonight, if anybody's counting. Nobody is.
fight.jersey: {winner} has the sweater over {loser}'s head and is just teeing off now. {loser} can't see where they're coming from.
Sweater over the head, and {loser} is fighting blind. {winner} empties the tank into the back of it.
{winner} yanks the jersey up over {loser}'s helmet and keeps swinging. That's the oldest move there is.
fight.knockdown: {winner} lands the big one and {loser} goes down flat. The linesmen step in now that it's safe.
A right hand, and {loser} is on the ice looking at the lights. {winner} stands over him for a while.
{loser} goes down in stages. {winner} helps him the rest of the way.
fight.linesmen: The linesmen finally get in between them, {winner} still swinging over the top.
They're pulled apart. {winner} got the better of that one by a distance, and {loser} knows it.
Linesmen step in and haul them off each other. {loser} is bleeding from somewhere, {winner} from nowhere.
fight.result: {winner} takes it. {loser} takes five, and the {winnerTeam} go on the power play for winning a fistfight, which is the CPhL rulebook in one sentence.
It's {winner}. {loser} is helped up and sent away, and his team pays for it with a man.
{winner} wins the fight and wins his side the man advantage. Whoever wrote these rules wasn't well.
final: That's the game. {leader} win it, {homeScore} to {awayScore}, and everyone still standing gets to go home.
Final score, {away} {awayScore} and {home} {homeScore}. {leader} with the win.
Horn goes. {leader} take it {homeScore}–{awayScore}, and the cleanup crew earn theirs tonight.
goal: IN. {shooter} beats {goalie}, and the horn does what the horn does.
{shooter} buries it. {assist} with the pass, and this building has come apart.
He shoots. HE SCORES. {shooter}, from {assist}, and {goalie} never had it.
goal.en: Empty net, and {shooter} buries it from his own blue line. {home} {homeScore}, {away} {awayScore}. Turn the lights off on your way out.
Into the empty cage. {shooter}. That's the gamble, and it didn't pay.
{shooter} finds the empty net. The goalie is on the bench watching it happen from sixty feet.
goal.pp: On the power play, {shooter} makes them pay for it. Man advantage, man in the net.
{team} cash the power play. {shooter} with the finish. That penalty cost exactly what penalties cost.
Extra man, extra goal. {shooter}, and {goalie} was hung out to dry.
goal.sh: SHORTHANDED! Down a man and {shooter} goes the other way and scores. Someone is getting shouted at.
A shorthanded goal. The {team} are a man DOWN and they've just gone ahead on it.
{shooter} scores while his teammate sits in the box. That's the most embarrassing goal in hockey.
hattrick: That's THREE for {player}. A hat trick in the CPhL, and nobody in this building owns a hat.
{player} completes the hat trick. Whatever they throw on the ice tonight, don't touch it.
Three goals, {player}. Remember the name, because at this rate he may not be with us long.
injury: {player} isn't getting up. He's helped off, and the {teamName} are down to {remaining} skaters, no replacement, that's the rule, and they wear it for the rest of the night.
That's {player}'s evening finished. {teamName} play the rest of this short.
{player} goes down the tunnel under his own power, barely. {remaining} left on the bench and nobody coming over the boards to help.
injury.report: Before we drop it: {count} out of the lineup tonight. {missing}, all still on the shelf from what was done to them, and up from the reserve, {callups}.
The injury list, and it's long: {missing}. Dressing instead: {callups}. Best of luck to them, sincerely, they'll need it.
{missing} not in the building tonight, or not in a state to be. {callups} get the sweaters. Nobody has asked them if they want them.
No {player} tonight, still out, and the club brings up {callup}. This league doesn't do get-well cards.
{count} missing between these two. That's the CPhL in the back half of a season: eventually everybody is somebody's replacement.
injury.sever: And {wound} isn't attached to him any more. It's over by the boards.
That's {wound}, lying a few feet from {player}. They're bringing out the stretcher and a bag.
{player} has left {wound} on the ice. The trainer picks it up and follows the stretcher off.
injury.wound: That's {wound}, by the look of how he's holding himself.
The trainer's calling it {wound} before he's even off the ice.
Word from the bench is {wound}. He'll be on the shelf a while.
intermission.casualties: Off the ice this period and not coming back: {casualties}. Their side plays the rest of this short. That's the rule and nobody's ever changed it.
{count} man off in that period. {player} in particular isn't going to be right for a while.
We lost {casualties} in there. No replacements. That's how a game gets away from a club in this league.
intermission.goal: {shooter} for the {team}, {clock} on the clock. {assist} with the helper.
intermission.intro: End of the {sectionOrd}, and they'll be fifteen minutes resurfacing what's left of it. Let's go back through it.
That's the horn. While they scrape it, here's your {sectionOrd} period.
Intermission. {away} {awayScore}, {home} {homeScore}, and here's how we got there.
intermission.outro: Back in a moment for the {nextOrd}. Don't go anywhere. Statistically, something's about to happen to somebody.
That's your intermission. They'll be out shortly, most of them.
We'll take a break. When we come back there'll be fresh ice and the same problems.
intermission.scoreless: No goals in the {sectionOrd}. Forty minutes of hockey between two clubs and nothing to show anyone for it.
Scoreless period. Both goaltenders held up, which in this league mostly means both of them are still conscious.
Nobody scored. I'd call it a goaltending duel but I watched it and it wasn't.
intermission.stats: Shots in the period: {away} {shotsAway}, {home} {shotsHome}. {penalties} minor infractions called, which is fewer than were committed.
{shots} shots between them in that period: {shotsAway} for the {away}, {shotsHome} for the {home}. The officials found {penalties} penalties in there somewhere.
By the numbers: {shotsAway}–{shotsHome} on goal, {penalties} to the box, {hits} hits that I'd describe as deliberate.
Shot clock says {away} {shotsAway}, {home} {shotsHome}. There were {fights} fights, which is under the league average, which is a sentence I hate saying.
intro: Good evening from Coldwater and welcome to CLUSTER PUCK. I'm Tug Brennan, nobody made me do this, and we're under way.
CPhL hockey tonight, brought to you by whoever is still paying, and I have been told not to name them on air.
Evening. Tug Brennan with you. The scheduler says these two are playing, so these two are playing.
Welcome in. The ice is down, the lights are on, and the insurance has lapsed. Let's go.
matchup: Tonight the {away} come to town to face the {home}.
It's the {away} against the {home}, and one of these buildings empties out happy.
{away} at {home}. Somebody's night gets worse in the next hour.
The {away} in from out of district to meet the {home}. Sixty minutes, whatever's left of it.
matchup.records: The {away}, {awayRecord} on the season, into the barn against the {home} at {homeRecord}.
On the marquee: {away} ({awayRecord}) versus {home} ({homeRecord}). Somebody's record gets worse tonight.
{away} bring {awayRecord} in here. {home} sit at {homeRecord}. The scheduler doesn't care.
ot.intro: Level after sixty. SUDDEN DEATH, and in this league that isn't a figure of speech.
We go to overtime. First goal wins it. So does the first body.
Sixty minutes settled nothing, so now we find out the other way.
outro: That's CLUSTER PUCK. I'm Tug Brennan. Mind how you go, and mind what's on the ice.
For the CPhL, I'm Tug Brennan. There's another one tomorrow, because there's always another one.
Tug Brennan, saying goodnight from Coldwater. Nobody won anything permanent.
pbp.after.blocked: It squirts out to the point.
pbp.battle: Sticks and elbows in the corner.

{player} takes it out of his own end.
{player} wheels out from behind the net.

{player} beats the defence to the line.
pbp.fight.drop: The gloves are on the ice.
pbp.goal.celebrate: {shooter} goes down on one knee and fires the arrow.
{shooter} skates off with his arms up.
pbp.goal.mob: Gloves on his helmet. Lots of them.
pbp.out.blocked: Off a shin pad. That'll bruise.
Somebody lay down in front of it.

pbp.out.glove: {goalie} plucks it out of the air.
pbp.out.post: Hits the post and stays out.
pbp.won: {player} out of the pile with it.
penalty: {player} goes for {infraction}. {penaltyMin} minutes, and the {team} are down a man.
Arm's up. {infraction} on {player}. {penaltyMin} in the box.
That's {penaltyMin} for {infraction}. {player} has a sit down and a think.
{player} caught for {infraction}. The officials noticed that one, which isn't guaranteed.
penalty.fight: Gloves off. {fighters} have decided the scoreboard isn't settling this. Linesmen are giving it a count of five before they pretend to care.
And they go. {fighters}, right at centre ice, and nobody is in a hurry to stop it.
Here it is. {fighters}, sweaters up over the heads, and the building is on its feet.
penalty.major: {penaltyMin} minutes for {infraction}. That's a major, and {player} is done thinking about it.
A five for {infraction} on {player}. Even these officials couldn't let that go.
{player} gets {penaltyMin} for {infraction}. He knew what he was doing and he did it anyway.
powerplay.kill: Killed it off. Back to even strength.
Penalty killed, and the {team} bench is very pleased with itself.
They survive it. Back to five a side.
powerplay.start: Man advantage {team} for the next two minutes. Let's see if they can do anything with it.
Power play, {team}. This is where games get decided and hearts get broken.
pull: {teamName} pull the goalie. Down {down}, six on five, and the net is empty behind them.
Here comes the goalie to the bench. {teamName} going for it with the extra attacker.
Empty net at the far end. {teamName} are down {down} and out of patience.
rivalry.intro: Evening. Tug Brennan, and you know what tonight is. These two don't like each other and they have never needed a reason.
Welcome in. It's one of THOSE nights. The scheduler put these two together again and the building knew before I did.
Good evening from Coldwater, where the ice is down and both of these clubs turned up early to stand around looking at each other.
rivalry.matchup: {away} at {home}, and this one has history nobody wrote down. Bring a bucket.
The {away} and the {home}. There's no trophy for this and they'll both bleed for it anyway.
It's {away}–{home}. Whatever this is, it started before the records did, and the records don't exist.
{away} into {home}'s barn. Last time these two met the officials went home early.
scrum: Bodies in front now, sticks up, everybody shoving and nobody swinging.
It's a scrum in the corner. Four men, one puck, no dignity.
They're all in there kicking at it. This is most of hockey, if we're honest.
section.end: Horn goes on the {sectionOrd}. {away} {awayScore}, {home} {homeScore}, and the Zamboni comes out to hide the evidence.
End of the {sectionOrd}. They'll resurface it, which is optimistic.
section.start: Here we go with the {sectionOrd}. {away} attacking twice, {home} once more after that.
{sectionOrd} period under way. Two blasts from the official and the puck is down.
Fresh sheet, {sectionOrd} period. It won't stay fresh.
shootout.intro: Nobody died and nobody scored, so we're going to the shootout. Frankly it's a let-down.
To the shootout. One at a time, one on one, and the crowd hates it.
shootout.miss: No good. {shooter} tries to be clever and isn't.
shootout.winner: {winner} take the shootout {soAway}–{soHome} and the two points.
It's over. {winner} win it in the skills competition, which counts, apparently.
shot.blocked: Blocked. Somebody in a {team} sweater is going to feel that in the morning.
Down goes a defender in front and it never gets through.
{shooter} winds up and a shin gets in the way. That's the job.
shot.breakaway: {shooter} is GONE, nothing between him and {goalie}, and {goalie} stones him.
Breakaway! {shooter} in alone, and he can't finish it.
Loose in the neutral zone, {shooter} is away, one on one, and {goalie} wins it.
shot.glove: {goalie} SNAPS the glove shut on it. He didn't need to look.
Glove save, {goalie}, and he holds it up like he's proud of it. He should be.
{shooter} picks a corner and {goalie} picks it right out of the air.
shot.pad: Off the pad and into the corner. {goalie} kicks it away.
{goalie} gets a leg on it. That's all it takes.
Pad save. {shooter} will want that one again.
shot.post: IRON! {shooter} rings it off the post and the whole building makes a noise I'd describe as grief.
OFF THE POST. Half an inch. Half an inch, and {goalie} knows it.
CLANG. That's the sound of a man's night changing and not changing at the same time.
shot.save: {goalie} takes it in the chest and holds on.
Shot away, and {goalie} has it. Nothing doing.
Straight into the logo. {goalie} barely moved.
shot.wide: Wide, and it rings around the boards.
{shooter} misses the net entirely. The glass takes it.
Off the mark. That one's going in the third row.
chatter.district: The Goons' lobby has a gun rack. Coats and firearms, same counter, same attendant, one ticket.
The crowd here doesn't cheer. It gets quieter, and every visiting club will tell you that's worse.
District 9 numbers its streets and not its buildings. The away bus parks with its engine running.
chatter.westside: The Glasshouse barn has a climate curtain over every door and the coldest ice in the league. The seats are heated.
Season tickets at Westside are inherited. There's a waiting list, and it's mostly lawyers.
Westside warm up to a string quartet. Same four players for eleven years. They wear earplugs for the third period.
chatter.boomtown: The Boomtown barn was a foundry. Some nights you can still smell the casting sand.
Every Bulldogs home game starts with the anvil. A man in an apron hits it once and the building goes quiet.
The rail along the boards here is pipe from the old works, painted orange. It rings when somebody goes into it.
chatter.marquee: The Marquee barn shares a wall with a nightclub. Third period, you can feel the bass through the glass.
Half the crowd at the Marquee came out in costume for something else. They stay for the fights.
The scoreboard here used to be a cinema sign. Two of its letters have been missing for forty years.
chatter.coldwater: The Highlanders walk out to a piper. He isn't good. He's played every home game for fourteen years.
Marrow Street pulls its shutters down an hour before puck drop. Everybody on it is in here.
The Highlanders' sweaters are woven on a loom above a chip shop on Marrow Street. It's a real clan sett, the Malcolm.
chatter.yards: The Yards barn is a cold store with seats bolted in. The ice was here first.
The tannoy here came out of a freight shed. In the second intermission it still reads out bay numbers.
chatter.st: The Guillotines are Father Jerome's club. He blesses the ice before the drop, and the ice crew waits until he's done.
The home bench at St Garneau's is two pews out of the nave, bolted to the boards.
Every Guillotines sweater goes through the Sisters of St Garneau's laundry on a Monday. The stains mostly come out.
Father Jerome never misses a home game. He sits by the door, and he watches it more than the ice.
